title: KPZ scaling in one-dimensional arrays of photon condensates
abstract: Bose-Einstein condensates of photons in dye filled microcavities are known to feature many properties of the ideal bose gas at thermal equilibrium. Nevertheless, the finite photon life time renders them driven dissipative systems where losses are balanced by continuous driving by a pump laser. We show here with simulations based on a classical field model that their driven-dissipative nature causes their first order coherence to feature Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling, a phenomenon well known in the related condensates of exciton-polaritons. Remarkably, we find that the KPZ scaling even occurs in a regime with large density fluctuations. We discuss the modification of the scaling by the occupation of excited states and how to recover the universal scaling behavior by spectral filtering.
summary: This work analyzes the coherence decay in photon condensates, which are driven-dissipative quantum systems. The authors demonstrate that the phase dynamics fall into the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) universality class, a finding robust even when density fluctuations are large. The research highlights the importance of spectral filtering in revealing the underlying universal physics.
main_problem: The study investigates whether the phase dynamics of driven-dissipative photon condensates exhibit Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling, particularly in regimes characterized by large density fluctuations.
main_result: The first-order coherence decay confirms KPZ scaling, even in the large density fluctuation (grand canonical) regime, although achieving the universal scaling requires spectral filtering.
method: The analysis combines deriving continuum equations from a classical field model with numerical simulations and analytical comparison of scaling exponents.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as photon condensates in a 1D array of dye-filled microcavities, treated as a driven-dissipative system coupled to excited molecular states.
key_observables: First-order coherence decay, spatiotemporal coherence $g^{(1)}(\Delta x, \Delta t)$, and the scaling function for phase fluctuations.
important_parameters: The analysis distinguishes between the large density fluctuation (grand canonical) and small density fluctuation (canonical) regimes.
main_assumptions: Initial approximations assume small density fluctuations for analytical derivations, but the numerical work extends to the large fluctuation regime. Spectral filtering is used to recover universal scaling.
figures_summary: Figures show the spatiotemporal first-order coherence decay, demonstrating collapse onto the universal KPZ scaling curve, especially after applying a spectral filter.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical model (driven-dissipative system) to deriving the phase dynamics, confirming KPZ scaling numerically in the grand canonical regime, and finally discussing the necessity of spectral filtering to recover universal behavior.
why_interesting: It connects non-equilibrium dynamics in quantum optics (photon BEC) to a universal critical phenomenon (KPZ scaling), providing insights into how dissipation and driving affect universal scaling laws in many-body systems.
